paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Jesus is walking ahead toward Jerusalem, and He tells the Twelve exactly what's coming: mocking, spitting, flogging, death, and rising again after three days (Mark 10:33-34). Then James and John walk up and ask for the best seats in the house (Mark 10:37). They heard the same words as everybody else, and somehow they're out here picking chairs! I think we all get a little too excited about our own spot sometimes, and I have been that stamper too.

Jesus doesn't shame them. He tells them, "You do not know what you are asking," and then He turns the whole idea of greatness upside down (Mark 10:38). The rulers of the Gentiles lord it over people, but He says, "it shall not be this way among you" (Mark 10:42-43). "Whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant, and whoever wants to be first must be the slave of all" (Mark 10:43-44). In Jesus' kingdom, the way up is down, and the biggest apron belongs to the one serving the most.

And Jesus doesn't just say it, He lives it. "For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many" (Mark 10:45). The One who deserves every seat in the room came to give His life for us. So here's what that means for you, baker: you don't have to fight for a place, because the One who served you already gave everything. Now you get to look around today and ask who you can serve.
